body:
Weremantis Guard (Human Form) CR 3

He’s not undead, but the farmer shuffling toward you looks like he could be. Emaciated, dressed in near-rags, and obviously afraid of the woman ordering him around, Not a threat — until he raises a serviceable sickle and picks up speed.

XP 800
Human kavraen (afflicted) weremantis warrior 1/expert 1
N Medium humanoid (human, shapechanger)
Init +0; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +3

DEFENSE

AC 10, touch 10, flat-footed 10
hp 11 (1d6+1d8+2)
Fort +3, Ref +0, Will +4

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee pitchfork (spear) +0 (1d8), club +0 (1d6), or knife +0 (1d4)
Ranged club +0 (1d6); unlikely to throw knife for fear of losing it

STATISTICS

Str 11, Dex 10, Con 12, Int 10, Wis 15, Cha 7
Base Atk +1; CMB +0; CMD 10
Feats Animal Affinity, Skill Focus (Profession [farmer])
Skills Craft (carpentry) +5, Handle Animal +5, Heal +6, Knowledge (local) +4, Knowledge (nature) +4, Perception +3, Profession (farmer) +10, Ride +7, Stealth +0
Languages Common
SQ change shape (human, hybrid, and giant mantis; polymorph), inhuman appearance, lycanthropic empathy (mantids and giant mantids)

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate forest
Organization solitary
Gear knife plus maybe club or pitchfork, not much else

Prisoners (escaped or otherwise), prison guards, hunters, farmers, and explorers are all taken captive by the weremantids at times. Since the captives are decidedly disposable, their weremantis captors don’t clothe or arm them, so they wear tattered clothing, and even when given tasks like patrolling the forest, they carry makeshift weapons or whatever farm implements or other gear they can scrounge. It would probably be easy for the captives to escape, but the fear of turning into mindless giant insects and devastating their homes and murdering their loved ones keeps them in despondent captivity in the Gardens of White.
